messages.author: c05fcdc4ef96c903
messages.subject: Getting error while running unmarkedFramePcount
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to use unmarkedFramePcount to generate the data which can be further used in pcount model (N mixture model). 

I am doing something like this:

mhb.y<-mhbdata[,"c.1"]     # this is the count of data across all sites in a year

elev<-mhbdata[,"elev"]
forest<-mhbdata[,"forest"]   # elevation and forest covariate



mhb.umf<-unmarkedFramePCount(y=mhb.y,
                             siteCovs=as.data.frame(elev, forest)) # there is no obscov in my data 

But after running this I am getting error:

Error in validObject(.Object) : 
  invalid class “unmarkedFrame” object: invalid object for slot "y" in class "unmarkedFrame": got class "integer", should be or extend class "matrix"

I would really appreciate any help in this regard.

Thanks
Sprih

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Getting error while running unmarkedFramePcount
parts:
Dear Sprih,

sounds like unmarked doesn't like the vector of counts "c.1". Try to make it a matrix:

mhb.y<-as.matrix(mhbdata[,"c.1"])

Please note that while it is technically possible to obtain estimates under the Nmix model for single-visit data (as you seem to be about to analyse in the example below), these estimates are extremely sensitive to parametric assumption, in an unhealthy way.

See attached paper on this topic.

Best regards  --- Marc

And I have read this paper and to be honest I didn't know whom to ask exactly but since you bought this up, can you suggest me what's the best way of analyzing my data then? It's a bird count on transect and I have different habitat covariates which I deduced from Arcmap.

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Getting error while running unmarkedFramePcount
parts:
Dear Sprih

if you have replicated your single-visit counts over multiple years, then you do have more information about abundance and detection and you could use the Dail-Madsen model (unmarked function pcountOpen, see here http://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/unmarked/versions/0.11-0/topics/pcountOpen).

Otherwise (i.e., if you want to analyse the data from each year individually) I personally would just fit a Poisson GL(M)M and acknowledge that what you're modeling is the product of expected abundance and detection probability and try to add covariates that are correlated with detection probability (such as effort measures).

Best regards  --- Marc

PS: It's Marc, btw.
